prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State:diversion/prioritization/communication/recovery;Saffron confirms plans/deferrals/revised-intents;Brindle distinguishes surface/runway/downstream-airspace holds;Handling Resource Planner grades severity/suppresses recovery-duplicates;Ground Handling Dispatcher→Towbar. New part:
S639: Performance Analytics Warehouse may analyze anonymized patterns of legality constraints and recovery selections to improve disruption playbooks.
S640: The design allows coordinated recovery during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase while preserving the operator's commercially sensitive decision logic.
S641: Apron cleanliness and stand readiness checks are treated as operational prerequisites before any surface movement release is accepted into the departure sequence.
S642: The Ramp Control Lead defines the sweep areas by stand, taxilane, service road interface, and equipment staging zone so that each check has a clear spatial boundary.
S643: Ground Handling Dispatcher assigns qualified personnel to perform apron sweeps during planned turnaround milestones and after any event that may introduce foreign object debris.
S644: Foreign object debris checks cover paved stand surfaces, jet bridge wheel paths, towbar storage locations, belt loader positions, fueling lanes, and adjacent drainage grates.
S645: East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting surveillance cues, but visual confirmation remains required where sensor coverage is obstructed by parked aircraft or ground equipment.
S646: The Ramp Movement Board displays stand readiness status using time-stamped states that distinguish unchecked, under inspection, cleaned, blocked, and ready conditions.
S647: Ramp Control Lead sends the Apron Sweep Completion Note after the responsible sweep team confirms that the assigned apron area is clean, safe, and free of observed foreign object debris.
S648: Airport CDM Portal uses the shuttle count to confirm that remote-stand passenger transfer demand is consistent with stand readiness timing.
S649: The Airport CDM Portal records each stand readiness confirmation with the stand identifier, responsible organization, inspection time, readiness constraint, and confirming user identity.
S650: Identity Access Service restricts readiness confirmation privileges to approved ramp, handling, and airport operations roles to prevent unverified operational releases.
S651: Time Synchronization Service provides the common time reference for sweep records, readiness confirmations, and safety-related release decisions.
S652: When a sweep identifies debris, leaking fluid, damaged pavement, unsecured equipment, wildlife activity, or lighting damage, the stand remains unavailable until the hazard is removed or mitigated.
S653: Ground Handling Dispatcher updates the Handling Resource Planner when personnel, equipment, or cleaning vehicles are reassigned to restore a contaminated stand.
S654: The Ramp Control Lead reviews unresolved hazards against active turnaround demand before allowing pushback planning to continue for the affected stand.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
